title: Players with Good or Bad Playoff Schedules
brief: Which players' teams have strong or weak schedules in weeks 19 to 21 ending 2027-03-28, especially two-game weeks? It must say that this list is a tiebreaker between similar players and matters most for expensive players.
summary: For our league the playoff schedule (weeks 19 to 21, ending 2027-03-28) is only a tiebreaker between similar players. It matters most for the expensive players you pay a large part of your 200 USD for. Dallas and Memphis play a full 4-4-4. Minnesota has a two-game semifinal week and Cleveland has a two-game finals week, so Anthony Edwards and Donovan Mitchell are the early picks where the tiebreaker counts most.

paragraphs.text: The experts agree that the fantasy playoff schedule should only break ties between two similar players. It is the least important factor at draft time. Do not take a worse player because his team plays more games in weeks 19 to 21. It should not shape your build or your punt plan.

In our auction this means one order of work. First set your price list from 9-cat value. Then, only when two players sit at about the same price and fill the same need, take or bid a little harder on the one whose team plays more games in weeks 19, 20 and 21.

It matters most for early picks. One expert does not want his best player to have a two-game week in the semifinal or the final. For mid and late picks he barely thinks about it. In our league, apply the tiebreaker to the first-round players who each take a big part of your 200 USD. Mostly ignore it for players you buy at 1 to 10 USD, since you can stream around them on waivers.

Good schedules: Dallas and Memphis play 4-4-4, the full 12 games. Dallas also has a league-high 16 back-to-backs. Players who rest on back-to-backs may not get all 12 games, and Kyrie Irving could fall to 10. Oklahoma City, Boston and the Clippers play 4-3-4. Boston has three back-to-backs in those weeks. Golden State's schedule is rated good for a March 28 end. Washington has only one back-to-back.

Weak schedules with 10 games: the Lakers, Indiana and Brooklyn play 3-4-3. Miami plays 4-3-3 but has no back-to-backs. Houston plays 3-3-4. Philadelphia, Toronto and Portland each have three back-to-backs in the playoff weeks, which hurts players who rest.

Two-game weeks: Minnesota plays 4-2-4, and the two-game week starts March 15, which is our semifinal. Cleveland plays 4-3-2, with a two-game finals week starting March 22, and it has the most back-to-backs in the league. These are the schedules the experts warn about most.

On the good side, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Jayson Tatum play 4-3-4 and Cooper Flagg plays 4-4-4. If one of them is level with a similar player on your list, lean toward him. The schedule does not raise your price cap on any of them.

The two early picks with two-game weeks are Anthony Edwards (semifinal) and Donovan Mitchell (final). Edwards's note says his two-game semifinal week pushes him lower. If either one is level with a similar guard on your list, take the other guard. But if bidding on him stalls below your price and no similar player is left, buy him. Do not reach for him early.

Luka Doncic, Tyrese Haliburton, Kevin Durant and Giannis Antetokounmpo all play only 10 games. Tyrese Maxey has three back-to-backs. These are small minuses for breaking ties, not reasons to pass. Giannis's note calls Miami's schedule a small minus, softened by having no back-to-backs.

The experts disagree on how much a two-game week should cost a player. One expert says that in head-to-head leagues a two-game playoff week should drop a player down your board. Another says to move him down only a little, and only when choosing between similar players. A third calls schedules the least important factor and uses them only between equal players. A practical middle path for us: treat the schedule as a pure tiebreaker for most players. For an expensive Minnesota or Cleveland player, also count the two-game week as a small real minus when you set your top bid.

sections.heading: Team stacks and after the draft

paragraphs.text: Owning up to three players from one NBA team is fine. It is more acceptable if that team has no two-game week in the fantasy playoffs, and five is too many. Be careful stacking Minnesota (Edwards, LaMelo Ball, Gobert, McDaniels) or Cleveland (Mitchell, Harden, Mobley, Allen), because their two-game weeks fall in our semifinal or final.

Later in the season, cheap Dallas and Memphis role players are natural playoff streamers on 4-4-4 schedules. Use FAB, and remember the limit of 6 adds per week. Check back-to-back rest habits before you rely on anyone. Mitchell Robinson, Al Horford and Robert Williams sit back-to-backs, and Kyrie Irving might too, which takes away much of a good schedule.
If you still depend on a Minnesota or Cleveland starter late in the season, the last chance to trade him for a similar player on a better schedule is the trade deadline on 2027-03-04.
